features.name: Safari web extension that darkens pages
features.description: A Safari Web Extension with a content script injected on all sites at document start. It reads each page's computed colors (backgrounds, text, borders, links, inline SVG fills) and generates an override stylesheet. Light backgrounds become dark and dark text becomes light, while hue is preserved so brand colors and highlights still stand out. It watches DOM mutations so dynamically added content is also darkened. Injecting early avoids a white flash on load.
features.reason: This is the product's whole purpose. Safari Web Extensions run locally with no network access.

features.name: Global mode: Auto / On / Off
features.description: A segmented control for the default behaviour on every site. Auto darkens only when the device is in Dark Mode (the extension checks the prefers-color-scheme media query and reacts live when it changes). On always darkens. Off never darkens unless a site override says otherwise.
features.reason: Shown in the screenshots as the primary setting, and the listing says it is linked to system Dark Mode by default.

features.name: Per-website settings
features.description: Each host (for example wikipedia.org) can override three things: whether darkening is enabled (Default, Auto, On or Off), which theme to use, and whether to ignore the site's built-in dark mode. Each picker has a 'Default' option that inherits the global value. Sites appear in a list on the main screen and can be removed.
features.reason: Highlighted in the screenshots and listing as a key capability: enable on only a few sites, or disable on some.

features.name: Detect and respect native dark mode
features.description: Before darkening, the content script checks whether the page already has a dark appearance, for example a low-luminance computed body or html background, or a color-scheme dark declaration. If it does, darkening is skipped to avoid double inversion. A per-site option forces darkening even when a built-in dark mode is detected.
features.reason: Shown on the per-site screen. Without it, sites that are already dark would be ruined.

features.name: Built-in themes
features.description: A set of preset color schemes such as Dark (dark gray), Black (true black for OLED), Dim, a navy variant and a sepia-dark variant. Each defines background, text, link and image treatment. The listing mentions 20+; a free version can ship a smaller curated set.
features.reason: Theme selection appears in both the default and per-site settings.

features.name: Custom theme editor
features.description: Create, duplicate, rename and delete themes. Editable values are background color, text color, link color and image adjustments (dim or brightness for images). A live preview card shows a mock article with a headline, body text and a photo using the chosen colors. Uses the SwiftUI ColorPicker.
features.reason: Shown in a screenshot. It adds polish, but the app is usable with presets alone.

features.name: Theme export/import via file
features.description: Export a theme as a small JSON file through the share sheet, and import it with a document picker or by opening the file in the app.
features.reason: A share button appears in the editor. A local file transfer needs no server.

features.name: Extension toolbar popup
features.description: A popup opened from Safari's extension (puzzle) menu. It shows the current host with a quick Default/On/Off toggle and a theme picker for that site, and saves those choices as a per-site setting.
features.reason: This is the natural way to add per-site overrides while browsing, and the puzzle icon is visible in the screenshot's address bar.

features.name: Advanced settings
features.description: Global fine-tuning options such as image dimming level, contrast strength and whether to darken images/videos/iframes. Exact contents are not shown in the listing and are inferred.
features.reason: A row for it is visible, but the details are unknown, so keep it minimal.

features.name: Setup guide
features.description: Step-by-step instructions for enabling the extension: Settings > Apps > Safari > Extensions, turn it on, and allow it on All Websites. Shows whether the extension appears to be active, based on the last time the extension pinged the shared container.
features.reason: Safari extensions cannot be enabled programmatically, so users need guidance.

features.name: Shortcuts actions
features.description: App Intents to set the global mode (Auto/On/Off), toggle darkening, and set the mode for a given site. Results are written to shared App Group storage.
features.reason: Mentioned in the listing and works fully on-device.

features.name: Control Center control and widget
features.description: An iOS 18 ControlWidget toggle and a Home Screen widget that show and switch the global mode.
features.reason: Mentioned in the listing; local only, but secondary.

features.name: Focus Filter
features.description: A SetFocusFilterIntent so a Focus (for example Sleep) can force the global mode to On or Off.
features.reason: Mentioned in the listing; on-device, but niche.

features.name: iCloud settings sync
features.description: Syncs settings and themes across devices through the user's iCloud account.
features.reason: Requires an account and a remote server, so it conflicts with the no-account, on-device rule.

features.name: Report a broken website
features.description: Sends the URL of a badly darkened site to the developer.
features.reason: Requires network access and a server. Users can disable darkening per site instead.

features.name: Curated per-site fix updates
features.description: Developer-maintained CSS fixes for specific sites, delivered through updates.
features.reason: Depends on a reporting backend and ongoing curation. A free app can bundle a small static fix list instead, without any remote fetching.

flows.name: First launch and enabling the extension
steps: User opens the app and the setup guide appears
User follows the steps to Settings > Safari > Extensions and enables the extension
User grants permission on All Websites
On the next page load the extension writes a heartbeat to shared storage
When the app returns to the foreground it shows the extension as active and dismisses the guide

flows.name: Browsing with automatic darkening
steps: User loads a page in Safari
The content script runs at document start and reads settings (global and host override) through native messaging or cached extension storage
It resolves the effective mode; in Auto it checks prefers-color-scheme
If the page is already dark and ignore-built-in is not forced, it skips
Otherwise it analyzes computed colors, builds the override CSS from the effective theme and injects it
A MutationObserver handles new nodes; a media query listener toggles darkening when system appearance changes

flows.name: Disabling darkening on one site
steps: On a site that looks wrong, user taps the puzzle icon and opens the extension popup
User selects Off for this site
The popup saves a SiteSetting for the host to shared storage
The content script removes the injected styles immediately
The site now appears in the app's Website Settings list

flows.name: Creating a custom theme
steps: User opens the Themes tab and taps New Theme (or duplicates a built-in one)
User names it and picks background, text and link colors and image dimming
The preview card updates live
User goes back and the theme is saved
User assigns it as the default theme or to a specific site

flows.name: Sharing a theme
steps: In Edit Theme, user taps the share button
The app writes a JSON theme file and opens the share sheet
The recipient opens the file and the app imports it into My Themes after confirmation

flows.name: Toggling via Shortcuts or Control Center
steps: User runs the 'Set Dark Mode' intent or taps the Control Center control
The intent writes the new global mode to the App Group
The extension picks up the change on the next page load or storage change event

fields.name: mode
fields.note: Defaults to auto, which follows the system appearance

fields.name: defaultThemeId
fields.note: References a Theme; defaults to the built-in 'Dark'

fields.name: lastExtensionPing
fields.note: Written by the extension and used for the setup status display

fields.name: host
fields.note: Normalized registrable domain, e.g. wikipedia.org; unique key

fields.name: ignoreBuiltInDarkMode
fields.note: When on, darken even if the site is already dark

fields.name: id
fields.note: Stable ID; built-in themes use fixed IDs

fields.name: isBuiltIn
fields.note: Built-in themes are read-only and can be duplicated

fields.name: linkColor
fields.note: Optional; if absent, the original hue is preserved with adjusted lightness

data_model.storage: Codable JSON (or UserDefaults) in a shared App Group container so the app, extension handler, widgets and intents read the same data. The Safari extension gets settings through SafariWebExtensionHandler native messaging (local IPC, no network) and caches them in browser.storage.local for synchronous-ish access at document start. No iCloud, no network requests.

monetization.model: Free, no in-app purchases, no ads, no subscription
monetization.notes: The original is a 3,99 € one-time purchase with no subscription. The Sbu version gives every feature away free. iCloud sync and website reporting are dropped because they need an account or network access.
